feed.title: NPR Topics: Home Page Top Stories
feed.subtitle: Top stories in the U.S. and world news, politics, health, science, business, music, arts and culture. Nonprofit journalism with a mission. This is NPR.

entry.title: To Madvillainy and beyond: How Stones Throw Records created a galaxy of taste
entry.summary: From generational classics like J Dilla's Donuts to the star turns of Sudan Archives and Anderson .Paak, one small LA label has made history for 30 years — without losing its roots.

entry.title: Katie Zacharia is 'transitioning out' as press secretary, White House says
entry.summary: Katie Zacharia's first official day was on Monday.

entry.title: Hot flashes, night sweats, insomnia – OB-GYNS set new rules for menopause treatment
entry.summary: For the first time since 2014, the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists has updated its guidelines for the treatment of symptoms commonly associated with menopause.

entry.title: The new Elizabeth Holmes film blends fact, fiction and fraud
entry.summary: Nathan Fielder's new film about Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes blurs the lines between reality and fiction. The film can be genuinely gripping — but the truth might not be so ambiguous.

entry.title: Amid talk of public execution, public opinion on death penalty is split
entry.summary: A majority of Americans support the death penalty for people convicted of murder, but support becomes more divided when questions vary.

entry.title: Israeli settlers beat Palestinians and a U.S. photojournalist in West Bank attacks
entry.summary: Masked Israeli settlers attacked Palestinians as they were harvesting olives in the occupied West Bank on Friday, injuring several people including a photojournalist working for The Washington Post.

entry.title: Crowds throng New Delhi and wave Indian flags amid escalating protests
entry.summary: Protests have intensified over a review of voter lists that critics say is politically motivated and threatens to disenfranchise voters. The Election Commission and Modi's administration deny these allegations.

entry.title: Sally Rooney's books will no longer be sold in U.K. after Palestinian Action support
entry.summary: The Irish author said her books can no longer be sold in the UK after she pledged the royalties to a banned pro-Palestinian group.

entry.title: How much money has Musk given to Republican groups since July? The quiz knows
entry.summary: Plus, this week saw comings and goings at the White House, the revenge of a child (reality) star, and Elon Musk doing Elon Musk things.

entry.title: Do Americans own the president's papers? Appeals court to weigh in
entry.summary: The administration says papers created in the White House belong to Donald Trump, not to the American people. The case could ultimately end up at the conservative-leaning Supreme Court.
